core_obligations: From (RS) to the equivalence (proof lines 5108-5122): assuming (RS), every object of the category over the fibre product is of the form x_1 x_x x_2, and the morphism sets satisfy the displayed identification, so the comparison functor is a 2-fibre product of categories by the categorical description.
The middle implication (proof lines 5124-5125): the implication from surjective to small extension is immediate.

From the small extension case back to (RS) (proof lines 5127-5146): assuming the equivalence for small extensions, use the description of the 2-fibre product to identify a given object y with the data (x_1, x_2, x, a_1, a_2), compute the morphism set out of a test object z as the fibre product of the two morphism sets over the morphism set into x, and conclude that y is a fibre product of x_1 and x_2 over x; the reduction lemma then gives (RS) for all surjections.
proof_roadmap: Show that (RS) turns the comparison functor into a 2-fibre product.
Note that the surjective case implies the small extension case.
Conversely compute the morphism sets in the small extension case to identify the objects as fibre products, and appeal to the reduction to small extensions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of three formulations of the condition (RS): the original one, the requirement that the comparison functor from the category over a fibre product to the 2-fibre product of the categories over the factors be an equivalence for surjective maps, and the same requirement for small extensions (statement lines 5093-5106). The proof (proof lines 5108-5150) derives the 2-categorical form from the object and morphism descriptions, notes the trivial implication, and recovers the fibre product description in the small extension case by an explicit computation of morphism sets. H2: two directions with an explicit morphism set computation, written out in full.
